grade.rationale: The scanner's main repository flow is understandable, but several edge cases undermine correctness and reliability: path containment is unsafe on case-sensitive systems, baseline findings are filtered twice, staged deletions are reported as current findings, and subprocess handling can deadlock or leave processes running.

summary: The implementation has a coherent high-level structure and useful separation between scanning, parsing, reporting, and persistence. However, path-scope validation can escape the repository, baseline handling conflicts with the desired accepted-finding accounting, staged scans inspect deleted content, and subprocess/error handling needs substantial hardening. Coverage is unknown.

grade.rationale: Path containment, baseline classification, and staged-deletion behavior can produce scans outside the intended scope or materially incorrect results.
Responsibilities are divided into helpers, but the class combines process execution, Git snapshot construction, parsing, persistence, state transitions, and reporting, making changes risky.

Names and control flow are generally clear, and the Gitleaks argument comments explain important behavior, although some behavior such as scanning deleted files conflicts with the apparent staged-scan semantics.
Sequential pipe draining can deadlock, cancellation does not terminate child processes, and baseline parsing errors escape the structured unavailable-result path.
Direct dependencies on Process, filesystem APIs, environment variables, static clocks, and state stores make failure paths and platform-specific behavior difficult to test deterministically.

findings.title: Case-insensitive containment check can admit paths outside the repository
findings.description: The path-scope boundary is checked with OrdinalIgnoreCase on every platform. On a case-sensitive filesystem, a sibling path whose repository-prefix spelling differs only by case can pass this check even though it is not beneath the repository root. The scanner may consequently read and persist metadata for an unintended directory.
findings.recommendation: Use a platform-correct containment test based on Path.GetRelativePath, rejecting rooted results and results equal to or beginning with '..' plus a separator. Resolve symbolic-link behavior explicitly if the repository boundary is intended to prevent traversal through links.

findings.title: Passing the baseline to Gitleaks prevents accepted findings from being classified
findings.description: The baseline is supplied to Gitleaks as --baseline-path, which causes matching leaks to be omitted from its report. The code then tries to find those same report entries and mark them Accepted. Because the scanner has already removed them, accepted-finding counts and persisted accepted findings will normally remain empty.
findings.recommendation: Choose one baseline owner. If Quality Studio must report and persist accepted findings, scan without Gitleaks baseline filtering and classify returned findings locally. Otherwise, remove the local acceptance/counting logic and document that baseline entries are excluded rather than reported as accepted.

findings.title: Staged scans report secrets from files being deleted
findings.description: For every staged deletion, the implementation reads the file from HEAD and places that old content into the temporary scan tree. A secret removed by the staged change is therefore reported as if it were present in the staged snapshot, producing false positives and potentially blocking a change that removes a credential.
findings.recommendation: Represent the staged index exactly: omit deleted paths from the temporary tree and from the scanned-file count. If historical deleted content is intentionally audited, expose that as a separate mode or finding category instead of treating it as staged content.

findings.title: Sequential stdout and stderr reads can deadlock subprocesses
findings.description: The code waits for stdout to reach EOF before beginning to drain stderr. If Gitleaks fills the redirected stderr pipe while stdout remains open, the child blocks writing stderr while the parent waits for stdout, and the scan never completes. RunGitAsync repeats the same pattern.
findings.recommendation: Start stdout and stderr ReadToEndAsync operations before awaiting either one, await both concurrently, and then await process exit. Preserve stderr for diagnostic messages when the exit code is unexpected.

findings.title: Cancellation can leave Gitleaks running and leak its report file
findings.description: Cancellation of a stream read or WaitForExitAsync exits through finally without terminating the child process, and the Process instance is not disposed. The still-running child may continue consuming resources and writing the temporary report; cleanup can fail and is silently ignored.
findings.recommendation: Dispose the Process, and on cancellation or exceptional exit kill the full process tree when it is still running before cleaning up the report. Await termination after killing so cleanup has deterministic ownership of the temporary file.

findings.title: Malformed or unreadable baseline files bypass structured failure handling
findings.description: Baseline loading occurs after the exception-filtered resolver and scan block. JsonNode.Parse, File.ReadAllTextAsync, or fingerprint value conversion can therefore throw directly from ScanAsync instead of producing the unavailable SecurityScanResult used for scanner and report failures.
findings.recommendation: Load and validate the baseline inside the guarded operation, or add a dedicated catch that returns a precise structured failure such as 'The Gitleaks baseline is invalid.' Distinguish malformed baseline input from malformed scanner output in the reported reason.

findings.title: Staged file contents are corrupted by a text decoding and encoding round trip
findings.description: git show output is read through a StreamReader into a string and then written using text encoding. Files that are not valid UTF-8, contain a byte-order mark, or are binary will not be reproduced byte-for-byte in the temporary staged tree, which can cause missed or fabricated matches.
findings.recommendation: Capture git show stdout as bytes and copy those bytes directly to the destination file. Keep the separate text-capturing helper only for Git commands whose output is defined as textual path data.
